title.narrative: Emergency Health and Nutrition Assistance for Vulnerable and Crisis-Affected Populations in Dikwa, Jere and MMC LGAs of Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed six months project aims to provide immediate, ltbgtlife-saving health and nutrition serviceslt/bgt to vulnerable conflict-affected populations during the lean season in ltbgtDikwa, Jere and Maiduguri (MMC) LGAs of Borno Statelt/bgt. The intervention, implemented by a consortium of ltbgtCare Best Initiative (CBI) and Unified Culture Promotion Foundation (UNICFP)lt/bgt will respond to worsening health and nutrition conditions among children under five, pregnant and lactating women, and other at-risk groups, driven by seasonal food insecurity, recurrent flooding, protracted conflict, and the deterioration of basic services. Through integrated health and nutrition outreach, mobile medical teams, health facility support, and community-based case management, this project will reduce malnutrition, prevent disease outbreaks, and mitigate mortality during the lean season. Implemented over six months, the intervention will target approximately 25,000 individuals with essential health services and 15,000 with nutrition services. ltbrgtltbrgtBelow are the ltbgtkey health activitieslt/bgt that would be carried out concurrently: ltbrgtlt/pgtltolgtltligtIntegrated Primary Healthcare Services in three supported health facilities and three mobile health teams, providing immunization, antenatal and postnatal care, treatment of common illnesses, and mental health and psychosocial support in hard-to-reach areas. lt/ligtltligtDisease Surveillance and Outbreak Response, including cholera, malaria, and measles active case search, referral of complicated cases, and deployment of rapid response teams. lt/ligtltligtSexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) Services, covering antenatal care, safe delivery, postnatal care, and Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC), with trained staff and supply of delivery kits. lt/ligtltligtRisk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) through two teams, delivering house-to-house health education, hygiene promotion, and awareness on disease prevention, Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV), and Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH). lt/ligtlt/olgtltpgtCollaboratively, the following ltbgtnutrition activitieslt/bgt will also be focused on: ltbrgtlt/pgtltolgtltligtSupport to existing OTPs, including provision of supplies and staff to ensure treatment of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) among children under five. lt/ligtltligtActive Case Finding and Referrals by Community Nutrition Mobilizers (CNMs), using the family MUAC approach and linking children with SAM/MAM to OTPs and Stabilization Centers. lt/ligtltligtMaternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) Counseling and establishment of mother-to-mother/father-to-father support groups for improved IYCF practices.lt/ligtltligtIntegration of Protection/GBV Services, including GBV/PSEA awareness sessions, risk mitigation in nutrition facilities, and referral of women and girls to specialized services. lt/ligtlt/olgtltpgtThe project design emphasizes community engagement and local ownership. Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs) Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) and Community Nutrition Mobilizers (CNMs) will be trained and deployed in both LGAs to lead mobile outreach and RCCE. House-to-house awareness campaigns will prioritize AWD/cholera prevention, hygiene practices, mas MUAC screen, case referral and malaria control, especially in flood-prone settlements. Nutrition staff and volunteers will be capacitated to ensure quality service delivery, strengthening existing systems for sustainability. The theory of change is that if access to essential health and nutrition services through combined facility-based, mobile, and community platforms, while mainstreaming protection and GBV risk mitigation is expanded, then morbidity and mortality among displaced and host populations will be reduced. This intervention is directly aligned with the NHF 2025 Lean Season Allocation Strategy, which prioritizes integrated health and nutrition interventions in Borno State, ensuring lifesaving support for those most at risk during the lean season.lt/pgt
